questions.text: द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण 1.0 × 10⁻¹² Cm का कोई विद्युत द्विध्रुव x-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है। इस क्षेत्र में किसी क्षण 2.0 × 10⁴ NC⁻¹ परिमाण का कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र अनुप्रयुक्त किया गया है। विद्युत-क्षेत्र के अनुदिश एकांक सदिश (√3/2) î + (1/2) ĵ है। उसी क्षण द्विध्रुव पर कार्यरत बल-आघूर्ण का परिमाण है:
questions.text_english: An electric dipole of dipole moment 1.0 × 10⁻¹² Cm lies along x-axis. An electric field of magnitude 2.0 × 10⁴ NC⁻¹ is switched on at an instant in the region. The unit vector along the electric field is (√3/2) î + (1/2) ĵ. The magnitude of the torque acting on the dipole at that instant is:
questions.solution:
The torque on a dipole is given by τ = pE sinθ. The dipole lies along the x-axis, so p = 1.0 × 10⁻¹² Cm in the î direction. The unit vector of the field is (√3/2) î + (1/2) ĵ, which makes an angle of 30° with the x-axis (since cos30° = √3/2). Therefore sinθ = sin30° = 1/2. Thus τ = pE sinθ = (1.0 × 10⁻¹²)(2.0 × 10⁴)(1/2) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ Nm.

Wait — re-evaluating: the angle between dipole (along x) and the field unit vector (√3/2 î + 1/2 ĵ) is θ = 30°, so sinθ = sin30° = 0.5. τ = (1.0 × 10⁻¹²)(2.0 × 10⁴)(0.5) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ Nm. This matches option (B). However, if we interpret the angle as 60° (between dipole and field direction where the ĵ component dominates the perpendicular contribution), sinθ = sin30° = 1/2 giving 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ Nm. The correct answer is (B) 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ Nm. Option A is too small by an order of magnitude; options C and D are larger than the calculated value.
questions.topic: Torque on an Electric Dipole

questions.text: जैसे ही परिपथ में धारा का स्विच चालू किया जाता है, बल्ब का तन्तु तत्क्षण चमकता है क्योंकि:
questions.text_english: When the switch of the circuit is turned on, the filament of the bulb glows instantaneously because:

options.A: शक्ति स्रोत से आने वाले इलेक्ट्रॉन आरम्भ में रिक्त तन्तु से होकर तीव्र गति करते हैं।
options.B: तन्तु पुराना हो सकता है और इसका प्रतिरोध निम्न हो सकता है।
options.C: तन्तु के सिरों पर तत्क्षण विद्युत-क्षेत्र स्थापित हो जाता है जो इलेक्ट्रॉनों को धकेलता है।
options.D: तन्तु में मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रकाश की चाल से गमन करते हैं।

options_english.A: the electrons coming from the power source move fast through the initially empty filament.
options_english.B: the filament may be old having low resistance.
options_english.C: electric field is established instantaneously across the filament which pushes the electrons.
options_english.D: free electrons in the filament travel with the speed of light.

questions.solution: When a switch is closed, an electric field is established almost instantaneously throughout the circuit at nearly the speed of light. This electric field acts on the free electrons already present in the filament and sets them in motion simultaneously, causing the bulb to glow instantly. Option A is wrong because electrons from the source do not physically travel to the filament instantaneously. Option B is irrelevant to the instantaneous glowing. Option D is incorrect because free electrons drift much slower than light; it is the electric field signal, not the electrons, that propagates at the speed of light.
questions.topic: Drift Velocity and Electric Field in Conductors

questions.text: वेग v⃗ = v₀ î से गतिमान आवेश q का कोई कण चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B⃗ = B₁ĵ + B₂k̂ के प्रदेश में प्रवेश करता है। इस कण पर आरोपित बल का परिमाण है:
questions.text_english: A particle with charge q moving with velocity v⃗ = v₀ î enters a region with magnetic field B⃗ = B₁ĵ + B₂k̂. The magnitude of force experienced by the particle is:
questions.solution: The magnetic force is F⃗ = q(v⃗ × B⃗). With v⃗ = v₀ î and B⃗ = B₁ĵ + B₂k̂, the cross product v⃗ × B⃗ = v₀ î × (B₁ĵ + B₂k̂) = v₀B₁(î × ĵ) + v₀B₂(î × k̂) = v₀B₁k̂ + v₀B₂(−ĵ) = −v₀B₂ĵ + v₀B₁k̂. The magnitude of this vector is v₀√(B₂² + B₁²). Therefore |F| = qv₀√(B₁² + B₂²), which is option C. Options A and B do not correctly account for vector cross product rules, and option D has incorrect dimensional grouping.
questions.topic: Force on a Moving Charge in a Magnetic Field

questions.text: कोई छड़ चुम्बक आरम्भ में किसी एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र से समकोण बनाता है। इस चुम्बक को तब तक घूर्णित किया जाता है जब तक कि इस पर कार्यरत बल-आघूर्ण उसके आरम्भिक मान का आधा हो जाए। छड़ चुम्बक को जिस कोण तक घूर्णित किया गया है, वह है:
questions.text_english: A bar magnet is initially at right angles to a uniform magnetic field. The magnet is rotated till the torque acting on it becomes one-half of its initial value. The angle through which the bar magnet is rotated is:
questions.solution: Initially the magnet is at 90° to the field, so initial torque τ₀ = mB sin90° = mB. When the magnet is rotated by angle θ from its initial position, the angle with the field becomes (90° − θ), so the new torque is τ = mB sin(90° − θ) = mB cosθ. Setting τ = τ₀/2: mB cosθ = mB/2, which gives cosθ = 1/2, so θ = 60°. The magnet must be rotated by 60°, making option C correct. Options A, B, and D give cos values that do not equal 1/2.
questions.topic: Torque on a Bar Magnet

questions.text: ऋणात्मक चुम्बकीय प्रवृत्ति वाले पदार्थ होते हैं:
questions.text_english: The materials having negative magnetic susceptibility are:
questions.solution: Diamagnetic materials are repelled by a magnetic field and have a small negative magnetic susceptibility (χ < 0), because they weakly oppose the applied field. Paramagnetic materials have a small positive susceptibility, and ferromagnetic materials have a very large positive susceptibility. Non-magnetic is not a standard classification in this context. Therefore, the correct answer is (A) diamagnetic.
questions.topic: Magnetic Susceptibility and Classification of Materials

questions.text: जब किसी कुण्डली में धारा में स्थायी दर से 8 A से 6 A तक का 4 ms में परिवर्तन होता है, तब उसमें 1.5 V का वि.वा. बल (emf) प्रेरित होता है। इस कुण्डली का स्व-प्रेरकत्व का मान है:
questions.text_english: When current in a coil changes at a steady rate from 8 A to 6 A in 4 ms, an emf of 1.5 V is induced in it. The value of self-inductance of the coil is:
questions.solution: The self-induced emf is given by |e| = L|dI/dt|. The rate of change of current is dI/dt = (6 − 8)/(4 × 10⁻³) = −2/(4 × 10⁻³) = −500 A/s, so |dI/dt| = 500 A/s. Therefore L = |e|/|dI/dt| = 1.5/500 = 3 × 10⁻³ H = 3 mH. Option C is correct. Options A, B, and D give incorrect values that do not satisfy the formula.
questions.topic: Self-Inductance

questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं (क्षेत्रफल 2.5 × 10⁻³ m²) के बीच के विद्युत-क्षेत्र में 4 × 10⁶ Vm⁻¹s⁻¹ की दर से परिवर्तन हो रहा है। इस संधारित्र की पट्टिकाओं के बीच विस्थापन धारा है:
questions.text_english: The electric field in space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor (each of area 2.5 × 10⁻³ m²) is changing at the rate of 4 × 10⁶ Vm⁻¹s⁻¹. The displacement current between the plates of the capacitor is:
questions.solution: Displacement current is given by I_d = ε₀ × A × (dE/dt). Substituting: I_d = (8.854 × 10⁻¹²) × (2.5 × 10⁻³) × (4 × 10⁶) = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² × 10⁴ = 8.854 × 10⁻⁸ A ≈ 8.85 × 10⁻⁸ A. This matches option C. The other options are numerically inconsistent with this formula.
questions.topic: Displacement Current

questions.text: ऊर्ध्वाधरत: रखे किसी लम्बे सीधे तार से ऊपर की ओर कोई स्थायी धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस धारावाही तार द्वारा उत्पन्न चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं की आकृति है:
questions.text_english: A long straight wire is held vertically and carries a steady current in upward direction. The shape of magnetic field lines produced by the current-carrying wire are:

options.A: तार से त्रिज्यत: बाहर आती क्षैतिज सीधी रेखाएँ।
options.B: धारावाही तार से समान्तर सीधी रेखाएँ।
options.C: तार के चारों ओर संकेंद्री क्षैतिज वृत्त।
options.D: तार के चारों ओर समाक्ष कुण्डलिनी।

options_english.A: horizontal straight lines directed radially out from the wire.
options_english.B: straight lines parallel to the current-carrying wire.
options_english.C: concentric horizontal circles around the wire.

questions.solution: According to Ampere's law and the Biot-Savart law, the magnetic field due to a long straight current-carrying wire forms closed concentric circles in planes perpendicular to the wire. Since the wire is vertical, these circles are horizontal and concentric around the wire. Options A and B are incorrect descriptions of the field geometry; option D (helixes) would describe the field around a moving charged particle, not a straight wire.
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Straight Current-Carrying Conductor

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कक्ष ताप पर विद्युत चालक है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is an electrical conductor at room temperature?
questions.solution: Tin (Sn) is a metal and thus a good electrical conductor at room temperature. Mica is an insulator. Silicon (Si) is a semiconductor with a moderate band gap; it conducts partially but is not classified as a conductor. Carbon in its diamond form (C) is an insulator due to its large band gap. Therefore, option A (Sn) is the correct answer.
questions.topic: Classification of Materials Based on Conductivity

questions.text: किसी गोलीय दर्पण द्वारा उत्पन्न आवर्धन −2.0 है। उपयोग किए गए दर्पण तथा बनने वाले प्रतिबिम्ब की प्रकृति होगी:
questions.text_english: The magnification produced by a spherical mirror is −2.0. The mirror used and the nature of the image formed will be:
questions.solution: A negative magnification (m = −2.0) indicates that the image is inverted. An inverted image formed by a mirror is always real. A real, inverted, and magnified image is formed only by a concave mirror when the object is placed between f and 2f. A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image. Therefore the mirror is concave and the image is real, making option B correct.
questions.topic: Mirror Formula and Magnification

questions.text: सही कथन चुनिए:
questions.text_english: Choose the correct statement:

options.A: प्रकाश के फ़ोटॉन विवर्तन दर्शाते हैं जबकि इलेक्ट्रॉन विवर्तन नहीं दर्शाते हैं।
options.B: इलेक्ट्रॉनों में संवेग होता है जबकि फोटॉनों में संवेग नहीं होता है।
options.C: प्रकाश के फ़ोटॉन तथा इलेक्ट्रॉन दोनों ही द्वैत प्रकृति दर्शाते हैं।
options.D: सभी विद्युत-चुम्बकीय विकिरणों में फ़ोटॉन नहीं होते हैं।

options_english.A: Photons of light show diffraction whereas electrons do not show diffraction.
options_english.B: Electrons have momentum whereas photons do not have momentum.
options_english.C: Photons of light and electrons both exhibit dual nature.
options_english.D: All electromagnetic radiations do not have photons.

questions.solution: Both photons and electrons exhibit wave-particle duality. Photons show particle nature (photoelectric effect) and wave nature (diffraction, interference). Electrons similarly show particle nature (definite mass and charge) and wave nature (electron diffraction, as shown by Davisson and Germer). Option A is false because electrons also show diffraction. Option B is false because photons carry momentum p = h/λ. Option D is false because all electromagnetic radiations consist of photons.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Wave-Particle Duality

questions.text: किसी लाल प्रकाश पुन्ज और किसी नीले प्रकाश पुन्ज की तीव्रताएँ समान हैं। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?
questions.text_english: A beam of red light and a beam of blue light have equal intensities. Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: नीले पुन्ज में लाल पुन्ज से संख्या में अधिक फ़ोटॉन हैं।
options.B: लाल पुन्ज में नीले पुन्ज से संख्या में अधिक फ़ोटॉन हैं।
options.C: लाल प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य नीले प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य से कम है।
options.D: नीले प्रकाश पुन्ज में प्रति फ़ोटॉन ऊर्जा लाल प्रकाश पुन्ज की अपेक्षा कम है।

options_english.A: The blue beam has more number of photons than the red beam.
options_english.B: The red beam has more number of photons than the blue beam.
options_english.C: Wavelength of red light is lesser than wavelength of blue light.
options_english.D: The blue light beam has lesser energy per photon than that in the red light beam.

questions.solution: Intensity = (number of photons per second) × (energy per photon) = n × hν. Since both beams have equal intensity, n_red × hν_red = n_blue × hν_blue. Because red light has a lower frequency (ν_red < ν_blue), each red photon has less energy. Therefore, to maintain the same intensity, the red beam must contain more photons than the blue beam. Option A is incorrect because blue photons carry more energy. Option C is wrong as red light has a longer, not shorter, wavelength. Option D is incorrect because blue photons have more energy per photon.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photon Energy and Intensity

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): किसी एकवर्णी आपतित विकिरण के लिए, किसी दी गई धातु से उत्सर्जित फ़ोटोइलेक्ट्रॉनों की चाल शून्य से किसी निश्चित अधिकतम मान तक के परास में होती है।
कारण (R): प्रत्येक धातु का अपना निश्चित कार्यफलन होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): For monochromatic incident radiation, the emitted photoelectrons from a given metal have speed ranging from zero to a certain maximum value.
Reason (R): Each metal has a definite work function.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से उचित कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: photoelectrons emitted by monochromatic light from a metal do have speeds ranging from zero to a maximum value. The maximum speed corresponds to electrons emitted from the surface (losing no energy to collisions), while electrons from deeper layers lose energy in collisions and emerge with lower speeds. Reason R is also true: each metal has a fixed work function. However, R does not explain why speeds range from zero to a maximum — that range arises because electrons originate from different depths within the metal and lose varying amounts of energy. Therefore, both are true but R is not the correct explanation of A, making option B correct.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): द्विझिरी प्रयोग में यदि एक झिरी बन्द है, तो परदे पर अन्य झिरी के कारण विवर्तन पैटर्न दृष्टिगोचर होगा।
कारण (R): व्यतिकरण के लिए कम-से-कम दो तरंगों की आवश्यकता होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In double slit experiment if one slit is closed, diffraction pattern due to the other slit will appear on the screen.
Reason (R): For interference, at least two waves are required.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से उचित कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: when one slit is closed in a double slit setup, the single open slit produces a single-slit diffraction pattern on the screen. Reason R is also true: interference does require at least two coherent waves superimposing. However, R does not explain why a diffraction pattern is seen — diffraction is a single-slit phenomenon caused by Huygens' secondary wavelets spreading from within the same slit, not because of two waves. Assertion and Reason are both correct but R is not the explanation of A. The correct answer is option B.
questions.topic: Single Slit Diffraction and Double Slit Interference

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): अनुनाद पर कोई श्रेणी LCR परिपथ शुद्ध प्रतिरोधी परिपथ की भाँति व्यवहार करता है।
कारण (R): अनुनाद पर, X_L = X_C से ω = 1/√(LC) प्राप्त होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): A series LCR circuit behaves as a pure resistive circuit at resonance.
Reason (R): At resonance, X_L = X_C gives ω = 1/√(LC).
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से उचित कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: at resonance in a series LCR circuit, the inductive reactance X_L and capacitive reactance X_C cancel each other, making the net impedance equal to just the resistance R. The circuit thus behaves as a purely resistive circuit with current in phase with the voltage. Reason R is also true and correctly explains A: X_L = X_C gives ωL = 1/(ωC), so ω² = 1/(LC), yielding ω = 1/√(LC), which is the resonant angular frequency condition. Since R correctly explains A, the answer is option A.
questions.topic: Series LCR Circuit and Resonance

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक ऋणावेशित नहीं होता है।
कारण (R): नैज अर्धचालक (उदासीन) में मादित उदासीन पंचसंयोजक अपद्रव्य परमाणु क्रिस्टल जालक को अपना पाँचवाँ अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन दान करके धनात्मक दाता बन जाता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): n-type semiconductor is not negatively charged.
Reason (R): Neutral pentavalent impurity atom doped in intrinsic semiconductor (neutral) donates its fifth unpaired electron to the crystal lattice and becomes a positive donor.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित में से उचित कोड चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों गलत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false.

questions.solution: Assertion A is true: an n-type semiconductor has extra electrons but it is electrically neutral overall, because the donor atoms that release these electrons become positively charged ions. The total charge of positive donor ions and free electrons remains balanced. Reason R is also true and correctly explains A: the neutral pentavalent (donor) atom donates its fifth electron to the lattice and itself becomes a positively charged ion, so the overall charge of the crystal remains zero. This is precisely why the n-type semiconductor is not negatively charged. Therefore option A is correct.

(क) (i) डोपक (मादक) के प्रकार को पहचानिए तथा (ii) इस प्रकार बने अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक को पहचानिए।
(ख) अपद्रव्यी अर्धचालक में इलेक्ट्रॉन सांद्रता परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
In an intrinsic semiconductor, carrier's concentration is 5 × 10⁸ m⁻³. On doping with impurity atoms, the hole concentration becomes 8 × 10¹² m⁻³.
(a) Identify (i) the type of dopant and (ii) the extrinsic semiconductor so formed.
(b) Calculate the electron concentration in the extrinsic semiconductor.

key_points: Hole concentration increased after doping, so the dopant is a trivalent (acceptor) impurity — p-type dopant.
The extrinsic semiconductor formed is a p-type semiconductor.
Using the mass action law: n_e × n_h = n_i², so n_e = n_i²/n_h = (5 × 10⁸)²/(8 × 10¹²) = 25 × 10¹⁶/8 × 10¹² = 3.125 × 10⁴ m⁻³.

questions.solution: Since the hole concentration (8 × 10¹² m⁻³) after doping is much greater than the intrinsic carrier concentration (5 × 10⁸ m⁻³), the holes are majority carriers. This means the dopant added is a trivalent (p-type or acceptor) impurity such as boron or aluminium, and the semiconductor formed is a p-type semiconductor. To find the electron concentration, we apply the mass action law: n_e × n_h = n_i². Therefore, n_e = n_i²/n_h = (5 × 10⁸)²/(8 × 10¹²) = (25 × 10¹⁶)/(8 × 10¹²) = 3.125 × 10⁴ m⁻³. The electron concentration in the extrinsic (p-type) semiconductor is approximately 3.125 × 10⁴ m⁻³.
questions.topic: Extrinsic Semiconductors and Mass Action Law

questions.text: किसी द्विझिरी प्रयोग में दो झिरियों के बीच पृथकन 1.5 mm है। इन झिरियों को 600 nm और 400 nm तरंगदैर्ध्यों के मिश्रित प्रकाश द्वारा प्रदीप्त किया गया है तथा झिरियों से 1.5 m दूरी पर स्थित परदे पर व्यतिकरण पैटर्न का प्रेक्षण किया गया है। केन्द्रीय उच्चिष्ठ से उस बिन्दु की न्यूनतम दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए जिस पर दो तरंगदैर्ध्यों के व्यतिकरण पैटर्नों की चमकीली फ्रिंजें संपात करती हैं।
questions.text_english: In a double slit experiment, the two slits are 1.5 mm apart. The slits are illuminated by a mixture of lights of wavelengths of 600 nm and 400 nm and the interference pattern is observed on a screen 1.5 m away from the slits. Find the minimum distance of the point from the central maximum at which bright fringes of the interference patterns of the two wavelengths coincide.

key_points: Bright fringe position: y_n = nλD/d. For coincidence, n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂, so n₁ × 600 = n₂ × 400, giving n₁/n₂ = 2/3. Minimum integers: n₁ = 2, n₂ = 3.
Minimum distance y = n₁λ₁D/d = 2 × 600 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.5 / (1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m = 1.2 mm.

questions.solution: The position of the nth bright fringe is given by y_n = nλD/d. For two wavelengths to coincide, the positions must be equal: n₁λ₁D/d = n₂λ₂D/d, which gives n₁λ₁ = n₂λ₂, i.e., n₁ × 600 = n₂ × 400. Simplifying, n₁/n₂ = 400/600 = 2/3. The minimum integers satisfying this are n₁ = 2 and n₂ = 3. The minimum distance from the central maximum is y = n₁λ₁D/d = 2 × 600 × 10⁻⁹ × 1.5/(1.5 × 10⁻³) = 1800 × 10⁻⁹ / 10⁻³ = 1.2 × 10⁻³ m = 1.2 mm.
questions.topic: Young's Double Slit Experiment

questions.text: अपवर्तनांक 1.5 तथा वक्रता त्रिज्या 10 cm के उस समतलोत्तल लेंस की फोकस दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए जो 1.25 अपवर्तनांक के किसी द्रव में डूबा है।
questions.text_english: Find the focal length of plano-convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and radius of curvature 10 cm when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index 1.25.

key_points: Use lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n_lens/n_liquid − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). For plano-convex: R₁ = 10 cm, R₂ = ∞.

questions.solution: Using the lensmaker's equation in medium: 1/f = (n_lens/n_liquid − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). For a plano-convex lens, the curved surface has R₁ = +10 cm and the flat surface has R₂ = ∞. Substituting: 1/f = (1.5/1.25 − 1)(1/10 − 0) = (1.2 − 1)(0.1) = 0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 cm⁻¹. Therefore f = 1/0.02 = 50 cm. The focal length of the plano-convex lens when immersed in the liquid is 50 cm.

questions.text: किसी इलेक्ट्रॉन के हाइड्रोजन परमाणु की उच्चतर ऊर्जा अवस्था से निम्नतम अवस्था पर कूदान करने पर उत्सर्जित विकिरणों की न्यूनतम और अधिकतम तरंगदैर्ध्यों का अनुपात ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Find the ratio of minimum to maximum wavelength of radiations emitted when electron jumps from higher energy state into ground state of hydrogen atom.

key_points: Maximum energy (minimum wavelength) is emitted when electron falls from n=∞ to n=1: ΔE_max = 13.6 eV.
Minimum energy (maximum wavelength) is emitted when electron falls from n=2 to n=1: ΔE_min = 13.6(1 − 1/4) = 10.2 eV.
λ_min/λ_max = ΔE_min/ΔE_max = 10.2/13.6 = 3/4.

questions.solution: The wavelength of emitted radiation is inversely proportional to the energy of the photon (λ = hc/ΔE). The minimum wavelength corresponds to maximum energy, which occurs when an electron falls from n = ∞ to n = 1, giving ΔE_max = 13.6 eV. The maximum wavelength corresponds to minimum energy, which occurs for the transition from n = 2 to n = 1 (the first line of the Lyman series): ΔE_min = 13.6(1 − 1/4) = 13.6 × 3/4 = 10.2 eV. Since λ ∝ 1/ΔE, the ratio λ_min/λ_max = ΔE_min/ΔE_max = 10.2/13.6 = 3/4.
questions.topic: Bohr Model and Spectral Series of Hydrogen

(i) कुंजी K बन्द होने पर बल्ब P और Q की चमक की तुलना बल्ब S की चमक से कीजिए।

questions.text_english:
(a) In the given figure, three identical bulbs P, Q and S are connected to a battery.
(i) Compare the brightness of bulbs P and Q with that of bulb S when key K is closed.
(ii) Compare the brightness of the bulbs S and Q when the key K is opened.
Justify your answer in both cases.

key_points: (i) K closed: P and Q are in parallel with each other, and this parallel combination is in series with S. Current through S is more than through P or Q individually, so S is brighter than P and Q. P and Q glow equally since they have the same resistance.

(ii) K open: P is disconnected; only S and Q remain in series with the battery. S and Q carry the same current and thus glow equally bright, but both glow less brightly than S did when K was closed because overall resistance has increased.

questions.solution: When K is closed: P and Q are in parallel, and their parallel combination (resistance R/2) is in series with S (resistance R). Total resistance = 3R/2. Current through S equals the total circuit current, while P and Q each carry half of that. Since power ∝ I²R, S carries more current and is brighter than P and Q. P and Q are equally bright as they have the same resistance and carry the same current. When K is opened: P is cut off from the circuit. Only S and Q remain in series, each carrying the same current (total resistance now 2R). S and Q glow with equal brightness, but both glow dimmer than S did when K was closed.

(क) जब किसी पृष्ठ पर आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति किसी निश्चित निम्नतम मान से कम होती है तो प्रकाश-विद्युत उत्सर्जन नहीं होता है।
(ख) आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति न कि आपतित प्रकाश की तीव्रता फ़ोटोइलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम गतिज ऊर्जा को प्रभावित करती है।
(ग) आपतित प्रकाश की आवृत्ति (ν) और अंतक वोल्टता (V₀) के बीच वक्र एक सरल रेखा होती है, जिसकी ढाल (प्रवणता) h/e होती है।
questions.text_english:
Explain the following observations using Einstein's photoelectric equation:
(a) Photoelectric emission does not occur from a surface when the frequency of the light incident on it is less than a certain minimum value.
(b) It is the frequency, and not the intensity of the incident light which affects the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons.
(c) The cut-off voltage (V₀) versus frequency (ν) of the incident light curve is a straight line with a slope h/e.

key_points: (a) Einstein's equation: KE_max = hν − φ. If hν < φ (i.e., ν < ν₀ = φ/h), KE_max becomes negative, meaning emission is impossible.
(b) KE_max = hν − φ shows KE_max depends only on ν, not on intensity. Intensity increases the number of photons but each photon's energy hν remains unchanged.
(c) eV₀ = KE_max = hν − φ, so V₀ = (h/e)ν − φ/e. This is linear in ν with slope h/e.

questions.solution: Einstein's photoelectric equation is KE_max = hν − φ, where hν is the energy of an incident photon and φ is the work function of the metal. (a) If the frequency ν of incident light is less than the threshold frequency ν₀ = φ/h, then hν < φ, which would make KE_max negative. Since kinetic energy cannot be negative, no photoelectrons are emitted. (b) KE_max = hν − φ clearly shows that the maximum kinetic energy depends only on ν. Increasing intensity increases the number of photons per unit time but does not change the energy hν of each photon, so it cannot change KE_max. (c) The stopping potential V₀ is related to KE_max by eV₀ = KE_max = hν − φ, giving V₀ = (h/e)ν − φ/e. This is a linear equation in ν, and its slope is h/e.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

(i) परिनालिका के फेरों की त्रिज्या में वृद्धि की जाए,

questions.text_english:
(a) A charged particle q moving with a velocity v⃗ is subjected to a uniform magnetic field B⃗ acting perpendicular to v⃗. If a uniform electric field E⃗ is also set up in the region along the direction of B⃗, describe the path followed by the particle and draw its shape.
(b) How will the magnetic field inside a long solenoid be affected when:
(i) the radius of the turns of the solenoid is increased,
(ii) the length of solenoid as well as the total number of its turns are doubled?

key_points: (a) B⃗ is perpendicular to v⃗, causing circular motion in the plane perpendicular to B⃗. E⃗ is along B⃗, so it accelerates the particle along B⃗. Combined motion is a helix with increasing pitch — a helical path with increasing pitch (stretched helix).
(b)(i) The magnetic field inside a solenoid B = μ₀nI depends on n = N/L (turns per unit length), not on radius. So increasing radius does NOT affect B.
(b)(ii) If both L and N are doubled, n = N/L remains the same. So B = μ₀nI is unchanged.

questions.solution: Part (a): The magnetic field B⃗ is perpendicular to velocity v⃗, so it exerts a centripetal force on the charge, making it undergo circular motion in the plane perpendicular to B⃗. The electric field E⃗, being along B⃗, exerts a force on the charge along the direction of B⃗, accelerating it uniformly in that direction. The superposition of circular motion in one plane and uniformly accelerated motion along the axis results in a helical path with increasing pitch — the particle follows a helix that stretches progressively along the direction of B⃗. Part (b): The magnetic field inside a solenoid is B = μ₀nI, where n = N/L is the number of turns per unit length. (i) Increasing the radius of turns does not change N or L, so n and hence B remain unaffected. (ii) If both L and N are doubled, n = (2N)/(2L) = N/L is unchanged, so the magnetic field B remains the same.
questions.topic: Motion of Charged Particle in Combined Fields; Solenoid

questions.text_english:
(a) Differentiate between magnetic flux through an area and magnetic field at a point.
(b) A bar magnet is held with its length along the axis of a closed coil. Initially the south pole of the magnet faces the coil. If the magnet is moved towards the coil, explain how a current is induced in the coil and in what direction.

key_points: (a) Magnetic flux (Φ) is the total number of magnetic field lines passing through a given area, Φ = B·A cosθ; it is a scalar. Magnetic field (B) at a point is the force per unit charge per unit velocity, a vector quantity at a specific location.

(b) As the south pole moves toward the coil, the flux linking the coil increases. By Faraday's law, an emf is induced opposing this change (Lenz's law). The induced current flows in such a direction that the face of the coil facing the approaching south pole acts as a south pole (to repel), so the induced current flows clockwise when viewed from the magnet's side.

questions.solution: Part (a): Magnetic field B at a point is a vector quantity defined as the magnetic force experienced per unit charge moving with unit velocity perpendicular to the field. Magnetic flux Φ through an area is a scalar quantity given by Φ = B·A cosθ, where θ is the angle between B and the area vector. Magnetic field is a point property, while magnetic flux is associated with an extended surface area. Part (b): As the south pole of the bar magnet approaches the coil, the magnetic flux through the coil (directed away from the south pole, i.e., toward the coil) increases. By Faraday's law, the induced emf opposes this increase in flux (Lenz's law). The induced current must create a magnetic field opposing the increasing flux, meaning the face of the coil facing the approaching magnet must behave as a south pole (to repel the approaching south pole). Therefore, the induced current flows in a clockwise direction when viewed from the south-pole side of the magnet.
questions.topic: Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law

(ख) किसी संधारित्र को आवेशित करते समय विस्थापन धारा का अस्तित्व कैसे और कहाँ होता है, संक्षेप में व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) State any three characteristics of electromagnetic waves.
(b) Briefly explain how and where the displacement current exists during the charging of a capacitor.

key_points: (a) Three characteristics: (1) EM waves are transverse in nature — E and B are perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation. (2) They travel in vacuum with speed c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s. (3) They carry energy and momentum but require no material medium for propagation.

(b) During charging, conduction current flows in the wires. Between the capacitor plates there is no conduction current, but the changing electric field there gives rise to a displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) that is equal to the conduction current, ensuring continuity of current through the circuit.

questions.solution: Part (a): Three key characteristics of electromagnetic waves are: first, they are transverse waves in which the electric field E and magnetic field B oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of wave propagation; second, they travel in free space with a constant speed of c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, independent of the frequency; and third, they carry energy and momentum and can travel through vacuum without requiring any material medium. Part (b): During the charging of a capacitor, conduction current flows through the connecting wires. However, no actual charge passes between the plates. Maxwell introduced the concept of displacement current to resolve the discontinuity: as the charge builds up, the electric field between the plates changes with time, creating a displacement current I_d = ε₀(dΦ_E/dt) in the region between the plates. This displacement current is numerically equal to the conduction current in the wires, thus ensuring the continuity of the total current in the circuit.
questions.topic: Properties of EM Waves and Displacement Current

questions.text_english:
(a) Define 'wavefront' of a light wave. A plane wavefront is refracted from a convex lens. Draw the shape of the refracted wavefront.
(b) A plane wave travelling in a medium is incident on a plane surface separating this medium from a rarer medium. Draw a diagram to show refraction of the wave. Hence, verify Snell's law.

key_points: (a) A wavefront is the locus of all points in a medium that are in the same phase of vibration at a given instant. A plane wavefront after passing through a convex lens becomes a converging spherical wavefront (concave shape) converging at the focus.

(b) Using Huygens' construction for refraction at a plane surface from denser to rarer medium, the refracted ray bends away from the normal. From the geometry of the wavefront diagram, sin i / sin r = v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁, which is Snell's law.

questions.solution: Part (a): A wavefront is defined as the locus of all points in a medium which are vibrating in the same phase at a given instant of time. It is always perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. When a plane wavefront passes through a convex lens, the central portion of the wavefront travels through greater thickness of glass and is retarded more compared to the edges. As a result, the refracted wavefront becomes a converging spherical wavefront (concave shape) that converges at the principal focus of the lens. Part (b): To verify Snell's law using Huygens' principle: consider a plane wavefront AB incident on the interface between a denser medium (speed v₁) and a rarer medium (speed v₂). By the time the wavefront at A enters the rarer medium and travels a distance AC = v₂t, the point B in the denser medium travels BE = v₁t. The refracted wavefront CE makes an angle r with the surface. From the geometry: sin i = BC/AC_base and sin r = CE/BC_base, giving sin i / sin r = v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁, which is Snell's law.

questions.text:
(क) p-प्रकार तथा n-प्रकार के अर्धचालकों में बहुसंख्यक और अल्पसंख्यक आवेश वाहक क्या होते हैं?
(ख) किसी p-n संधि डायोड में विसरण धारा और अपवाह धारा निर्मित होने की संक्षेप में व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) What are majority and minority charge carriers of p-type and n-type semiconductors?
(b) Explain briefly the formation of diffusion current and drift current in a p-n junction diode.

key_points: (a) In p-type: majority carriers are holes; minority carriers are electrons. In n-type: majority carriers are electrons; minority carriers are holes.
(b) Diffusion current: holes from p-side diffuse to n-side and electrons from n-side diffuse to p-side due to concentration gradient, building up a depletion region and a barrier potential.

Drift current: the electric field in the depletion region drives minority carriers across the junction — minority electrons from p-side drift to n-side and minority holes from n-side drift to p-side. At equilibrium, diffusion current equals drift current.

questions.solution: Part (a): In a p-type semiconductor, holes are the majority charge carriers (created by trivalent dopant atoms accepting electrons) and electrons are the minority charge carriers. In an n-type semiconductor, electrons are the majority charge carriers (donated by pentavalent dopant atoms) and holes are the minority charge carriers. Part (b): When a p-n junction is formed, holes from the p-side and electrons from the n-side diffuse across the junction due to the concentration gradient. This movement of charge constitutes the diffusion current. As diffusion continues, a depletion layer is formed near the junction, producing a built-in electric field directed from n to p. This field opposes further diffusion and simultaneously drives minority charge carriers across the junction — minority electrons from the p-side are swept to the n-side and minority holes from the n-side are swept to the p-side — constituting the drift current. At equilibrium, the drift current exactly balances the diffusion current, resulting in zero net current.

(क) (i) मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉनों के संख्या घनत्व तथा विश्रांति काल के पदों में किसी चालक की प्रतिरोधकता के लिए व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए।
(ii) आरेख में दो भिन्न समय अन्तरालों में किसी तार की अनुप्रस्थ-काट से प्रवाहित धारा का ग्राफ दर्शाया गया है। इन समय अन्तरालों में इस अनुप्रस्थ-काट से प्रवाहित आवेशों (Q₁ और Q₂) की तुलना कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Derive an expression for the resistivity of a conductor in terms of number density of free electrons and relaxation time.
(ii) The figure shows the plot of current through a cross-section of wire over two different time intervals. Compare the charges (Q₁ and Q₂) that pass through the cross-section during these time intervals.

OR

(b) (i) A battery of emf E and internal resistance r is connected to a variable external resistance R.
(I) Obtain the expression for current I in the circuit and the value of maximum current the battery can supply.
(II) Obtain the terminal voltage V across the battery and its maximum possible value.
(ii) The above battery sends a current I₁ when R = R₁ and a current I₂ when R = R₂. Obtain the internal resistance of the battery in terms of I₁, I₂, R₁ and R₂.

key_points: (a)(i) Drift velocity v_d = eEτ/m. Current density J = nev_d = ne²Eτ/m. Resistivity ρ = E/J = m/(ne²τ).
(a)(ii) Charge = area under I-t graph. Q₁ = 2 × 2 = 4 C (rectangle from t=1 to t=3). Q₂ = (1/2) × 4 × 2 = 4 C (triangle from t=5 to t=9). So Q₁ = Q₂.
(b)(i)(I) I = E/(R+r); maximum current when R→0: I_max = E/r. (b)(i)(II) V = IR = ER/(R+r); maximum V when R→∞: V_max = E.
(b)(ii) E = I₁(R₁+r) and E = I₂(R₂+r). Subtracting and solving: r = (I₁R₁ − I₂R₂)/(I₂ − I₁).

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): In a conductor under electric field E, electrons experience acceleration a = eE/m. The average drift velocity is v_d = aτ = eEτ/m, where τ is the relaxation time. Current density J = nev_d = ne²Eτ/m. Since resistivity ρ = E/J, we get ρ = m/(ne²τ). Part (a)(ii): The charge is the area under the I-t graph. For Q₁ (rectangle): Q₁ = I × Δt = 2 × 2 = 4 C. For Q₂ (triangle): Q₂ = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 4 × 2 = 4 C. Therefore Q₁ = Q₂. Part (b)(i)(I): Applying Kirchhoff's voltage law: E = I(R + r), so I = E/(R + r). Maximum current is obtained when R = 0: I_max = E/r. Part (b)(i)(II): Terminal voltage V = E − Ir = ER/(R + r). As R → ∞, V → E, so V_max = E. Part (b)(ii): E = I₁(R₁ + r) and E = I₂(R₂ + r). Subtracting: I₁R₁ + I₁r = I₂R₂ + I₂r. Rearranging: r(I₁ − I₂) = I₂R₂ − I₁R₁. Therefore r = (I₂R₂ − I₁R₁)/(I₁ − I₂) = (I₁R₁ − I₂R₂)/(I₂ − I₁).

questions.text: किसी हाइड्रोजन परमाणु में परमाणु के नाभिक पर स्थित प्रोटॉन के चारों ओर त्रिज्या r की वृत्ताकार कक्षा में कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन किसी निश्चित चाल v से परिक्रमा करता है। प्रोटॉन और परिक्रमी इलेक्ट्रॉन के बीच लगने वाला स्थिर-विद्युत आकर्षण बल इलेक्ट्रॉन को कक्षा में परिक्रमण करने के लिए आवश्यक अभिकेन्द्र बल प्रदान करता है। बोर मॉडल के अनुसार, एक इलेक्ट्रॉन निश्चित स्थायी कक्षाओं में ही परिक्रमण कर सकता है। इन कक्षाओं में इलेक्ट्रॉन का कोणीय संवेग h/2π का कोई पूर्णांक गुणज होता है, जहाँ h प्लांक स्थिरांक है। साथ ही, जब कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन उच्च ऊर्जा की कक्षा से निम्न ऊर्जा की कक्षा में संक्रमण करता है, तो कोई फ़ोटॉन उत्सर्जित होता है जिसकी ऊर्जा अंतिम अवस्था से प्रारम्भिक अवस्था की ऊर्जाओं के बीच अन्तर के बराबर होती है। यह मानते हुए कि इलेक्ट्रॉन का द्रव्यमान तथा आवेश क्रमशः m और e हैं, निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
questions.text_english: A hydrogen atom consists of an electron revolving in a circular orbit of radius r with certain velocity v around a proton located at the nucleus of the atom. The electrostatic force of attraction between the revolving electron and the proton provides the requisite centripetal force to keep it in the orbit. According to Bohr's model, an electron can revolve only in certain stable orbits. The angular momentum of the electron in these orbits is some integral multiple of h/2π, where h is the Planck's constant. Further, when an electron makes a transition from one orbit of higher energy to that of lower energy, a photon is emitted having energy equal to the difference between energies of the initial and final states. Assuming the mass and charge of an electron as m and e respectively, answer the following questions.

sub_questions.text: कक्षा की त्रिज्या (r) तथा भौतिक नियतांक (K = 1/4πε₀) के पदों में इलेक्ट्रॉन की चाल v के लिए व्यंजक है:
sub_questions.text_english: The expression for the speed of electron v in terms of radius of the orbit (r) and physical constant (K = 1/4πε₀) is:
sub_questions.solution: The centripetal force is provided by the electrostatic attraction: Ke²/r² = mv²/r. Solving for v²: v² = Ke²/(mr). Therefore v = √(Ke²/mr), which is option C.

sub_questions.text: r और भौतिक नियतांक K के पदों में परमाणु की कुल ऊर्जा है:
sub_questions.text_english: The total energy of the atom in terms of r and physical constant K is:
sub_questions.solution: KE = (1/2)mv² = Ke²/(2r). PE = −Ke²/r. Total energy E = KE + PE = Ke²/(2r) − Ke²/r = −Ke²/(2r). The total energy is negative, confirming the electron is bound. Option B is correct.

sub_questions.text: किसी परमाणु में जब कोई इलेक्ट्रॉन एक अवस्था से दूसरी अवस्था में संक्रमण करता है, तो 500 nm तरंगदैर्ध्य का कोई फ़ोटॉन उत्सर्जित होता है। तब बोर मॉडल के अनुसार eV में इलेक्ट्रॉन की कुल ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन तथा इलेक्ट्रॉन की गतिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन क्रमशः होंगे:
sub_questions.text_english: A photon of wavelength 500 nm is emitted when an electron makes a transition from one state to the other state in an atom. The change in the total energy of the electron and change in its kinetic energy in eV as per Bohr's model, respectively will be:
sub_questions.solution: Photon energy = hc/λ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3 × 10⁸)/(500 × 10⁻⁹) = 3.978 × 10⁻¹⁹ J ≈ 2.48 eV. This energy is emitted, so the total energy of the atom decreases by 2.48 eV: ΔE_total = −2.48 eV. In Bohr's model, KE = −(Total Energy), so ΔKE = +2.48 eV. The answer is option C: −2.48, +2.48.

sub_questions.text:
(क) हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर मॉडल में इलेक्ट्रॉन की nवीं कक्षा में परिक्रमण की आवृत्ति निम्नलिखित में से किसके आनुपातिक होती है?

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) In Bohr's model of hydrogen atom, the frequency of revolution of electron in its nth orbit is proportional to:
OR
(b) An electron makes a transition from −3.4 eV state to the ground state in hydrogen atom. Its radius of orbit changes by: (radius of orbit of electron in ground state = 0.53 Å)
sub_questions.solution: Part (a): The orbital frequency f = v/(2πr). In Bohr's model, r ∝ n² and v ∝ 1/n, so f ∝ (1/n)/n² = 1/n³. Answer is D (1/n³). Part (b): E_n = −13.6/n² eV. For −3.4 eV: n² = 13.6/3.4 = 4, so n = 2. Ground state has n=1. Radius r_n = n²r₁ = n² × 0.53 Å. For n=2: r₂ = 4 × 0.53 = 2.12 Å. Change in radius = r₂ − r₁ = 2.12 − 0.53 = 1.59 Å. Wait — the question asks for the change from the −3.4 eV state (n=2, r=2.12 Å) to ground state (n=1, r=0.53 Å): Δr = 2.12 − 0.53 = 1.59 Å. Answer is C (1.59 Å).

questions.text: किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र में दो चालक पट्टिकाएँ होती हैं जो सामान्यत: किसी दूरी पर एक-दूसरे के समान्तर रखी होती हैं। जब किसी संधारित्र को आवेशित किया जाता है, तो आवेश पट्टिकाओं के भीतरी पृष्ठों पर स्थित हो जाता है तथा पट्टिकाओं के बीच कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र स्थापित हो जाता है। इस प्रकार संधारित्र में स्थिर-वैद्युत ऊर्जा संचित होती है। आरेख में तीन धातु की बृहत् वर्गाकार पट्टिकाएँ हैं जिनमें प्रत्येक की भुजा की लम्बाई 'L' है तथा ये एक-दूसरे के समान्तर और समदूरस्थ रखी हैं। P₁ और P₂ तथा P₂ और P₃ के रिक्त स्थान को परावैद्युतांक 'K' की अभ्रक की शीटों से पूर्णरूपेण भर दिया गया है। पट्टिका P₂ को बिन्दु A तथा अन्य पट्टिकाओं P₁ और P₃ को बिन्दु B से संयोजित किया गया है। बिन्दु B के सापेक्ष बिन्दु A के विभव को किसी धनात्मक विभव पर पोषित किया गया है तथा A और B के बीच विभवान्तर V है।
questions.text_english: A parallel plate capacitor consists of two conducting plates kept generally parallel to each other at a distance. When the capacitor is charged, the charge resides on the inner surfaces of the plates and an electric field is set up between them. Thus, electrostatic energy is stored in the capacitor. The figure shows three large square metallic plates, each of side 'L' held parallel and equidistant from each other. The space between P₁ and P₂ and P₂ and P₃ is completely filled with mica sheets of dielectric constant 'K'. The plate P₂ is connected to point A and other plates P₁ and P₃ are connected to point B. Point A is maintained at a positive potential with respect to point B and the potential difference between A and B is V.

sub_questions.text: A और B के बीच निकाय की धारिता होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: The capacitance of the system between A and B will be:
sub_questions.solution: P₂ is connected to A, while P₁ and P₃ are connected to B. This forms two capacitors: C₁ (between P₁ and P₂) and C₂ (between P₂ and P₃), both with the same plate area L² and separation d, filled with dielectric K. Each capacitor C = Kε₀L²/d. Since both capacitors share A (P₂) on one side and B (P₁ or P₃) on the other, they are connected in parallel. Total capacitance = C₁ + C₂ = 2Kε₀L²/d. Answer is C.

sub_questions.text_english: The charge on plate P₁ is:
sub_questions.solution: P₁ forms one capacitor (C₁ = Kε₀L²/d) with P₂, connected between A and B with potential difference V. Charge on P₁ = C₁ × V = Kε₀L²V/d. However, since P₁ is connected to B (lower potential), it accumulates negative charge. The magnitude of charge on P₁ = Kε₀L²V/d. Wait — since total C = 2Kε₀L²/d and both capacitors are identical, each carries equal charge Q/2 = CV/2 where C_each = Kε₀L²/d. So Q on P₁ = (Kε₀L²/d) × V = ε₀KVL²/d ... re-checking: charge on each individual capacitor = C_each × V = (Kε₀L²/d) × V = Kε₀VL²/d. But option A is ε₀VKL²/2d. The total charge from A is 2Kε₀L²V/d which splits equally, giving each capacitor Kε₀L²V/d. P₁ on the B side has charge magnitude = Kε₀VL²/d = option B. But since both capacitors charge independently and P₁ is on side B, charge on P₁ = −Kε₀VL²/d magnitude. The correct option for magnitude is B (ε₀VKL²/d).

sub_questions.text: P₁ और P₂ के बीच के प्रदेश में विद्युत-क्षेत्र है:
sub_questions.text_english: The electric field in the region between P₁ and P₂ is:
sub_questions.solution: The potential difference between P₂ (at potential V relative to B) and P₁ (at B, potential 0) is V. The separation between P₁ and P₂ is d. The electric field between the plates (uniform, ignoring fringe effects) is E = V/d. Answer is A.

(क) इस निकाय के समान धारिता वाले वायु से भरे समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र, जिसकी पट्टिकाओं का क्षेत्रफल (L²) समान है, की पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन होगा:

sub_questions.text_english:

OR
(b) If the source of potential difference applied between A and B is removed, and then A and B are connected by a conducting wire, the net charge on the system will be:

Part (b): When the source is removed and A and B are connected, charge redistributes but the system as a whole (taking A and B plates together) was overall neutral before (equal and opposite charges on inner faces). The net charge on the entire system was zero initially and remains zero after redistribution. Answer: Zero. Both match option C for (a) and option D for (b). (a) (i) State Lenz's law and explain how this law is a consequence of conservation of energy principle.
(ii) A square shaped loop of side l/2 is initially lying outside a region of uniform magnetic field B as shown in the figure. The loop is moved towards right with a constant velocity v till it goes out of the region of magnetic field.
(I) What will be the directions of induced current when the loop enters the field and when it leaves the field?
(II) Draw the plots showing the variation of magnetic flux φ linked with the loop with time t and variation of induced emf E with time t. Mark the relevant values of E, φ and t on the graphs.

OR

(b) (i) Differentiate between peak and rms values of alternating current. How are they related?
(ii) A current element X is connected across an ac source of emf V = V₀ sin 2πvt. It is found that the voltage leads the current in phase by π/2 radian. If element X was replaced by element Y, the voltage lags behind the current in phase by π/2 radian.
(I) Identify elements X and Y by drawing phasor diagrams.
(II) Obtain the condition of resonance when both elements X and Y are connected in series to the source and obtain expression for resonant frequency. What is the impedance value in this case?

key_points: Lenz's law: The direction of the induced emf is such that if a current flows, it opposes the change in magnetic flux that caused it.
Link to energy conservation: The opposing force on the moving conductor means external work must be done to maintain motion; this work is converted to electrical energy — energy is thus conserved.
Loop entering field: flux increases into the page; induced current is anticlockwise (counterclockwise) to oppose increasing flux.
Loop leaving field: flux decreases; induced current is clockwise to maintain the flux.

φ-t graph: linearly increases from 0 to B(l/2)² while entering, remains constant while fully inside, linearly decreases while leaving. E-t graph: constant positive while entering, zero while fully inside, constant negative while leaving.

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): Lenz's law states that the induced emf in a circuit is always in such a direction that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it. This is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy. If the induced current aided the change in flux, it would create a self-sustaining system generating energy without any input — which is impossible. Instead, by opposing the cause (the change in flux), the system requires an external agent to do work, which is then converted into electrical energy. Energy input equals electrical energy output, satisfying conservation. Part (a)(ii): The square loop has side l/2. When the loop enters the field (B directed into the page): the flux through the loop increases in the inward direction. By Lenz's law, the induced current opposes this increase, so it flows anticlockwise (when viewed from above) to create a field out of the page inside the loop. When the loop leaves the field: the flux decreases; the induced current flows clockwise to maintain the inward flux. Part (II): The φ-t graph shows φ increasing linearly from 0 to B(l/2)² = Bl²/4 as the loop enters (time 0 to t₁ = l/(2v)), remains constant at Bl²/4 while the loop is fully inside (from t₁ to t₂ = l/v + l/(2v) = 3l/(2v)), then decreases linearly back to 0 as it exits (from t₂ to t₃ = 2l/v). The E-t graph shows a constant emf E = Bvl/2 during entry, E = 0 when fully inside, and E = −Bvl/2 during exit.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) An object is placed 30 cm from a thin convex lens of focal length 10 cm. The lens forms a sharp image on a screen. If a thin concave lens is placed in contact with the convex lens, the sharp image on the screen is formed when the screen is moved by 45 cm from its initial position. Calculate the focal length of the concave lens.
(ii) Calculate the angle of minimum deviation of an equilateral prism. The refractive index of the prism is √3. Calculate the angle of incidence for this case of minimum deviation also.

OR

(b) (i) A physics teacher wants to demonstrate interference with the help of double slit experiment using a laser beam of 633 nm wavelength. Since the hall is large enough, interference pattern is formed on the wall 5.0 m from the slits. For clear and comfortable view by all the students they want the fringe width 5 mm.
(I) Find the slit separation for obtaining the desired interference pattern.
(II) How far will the first minimum be from the central maximum?
(ii) A parallel beam of light of wavelength 650 nm passes through a slit of width 0.6 mm. The diffraction pattern is obtained on a screen kept 60 cm away from the slit. Find the distance between first order minima on both sides of the central maximum.

key_points: (a)(i) Convex lens alone: u = −30 cm, f₁ = +10 cm. Using lens formula: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f gives v = +15 cm. With concave lens added, new image distance v' = 15 + 45 = 60 cm (screen moved away). Combined focal length: 1/F = 1/v' − 1/u = 1/60 − 1/(−30) = 1/60 + 1/30 = 1/20. So F = 20 cm. 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ → 1/20 = 1/10 + 1/f₂ → f₂ = −20 cm.

(a)(ii) For equilateral prism, A = 60°. At minimum deviation: n = sin((A + D_m)/2)/sin(A/2). √3 = sin((60 + D_m)/2)/sin30°. √3 × 0.5 = sin((60 + D_m)/2). sin((60 + D_m)/2) = √3/2 = sin60°. So (60 + D_m)/2 = 60°, giving D_m = 60°. Angle of incidence: i = (A + D_m)/2 = 60°.
(b)(i)(I) Fringe width β = λD/d → d = λD/β = 633×10⁻⁹×5/5×10⁻³ = 633 μm ≈ 0.633 mm.
(b)(i)(II) First minimum is at β/2 = 2.5 mm from central maximum.
(b)(ii) Distance between first minima on both sides = 2λD/a = 2×650×10⁻⁹×0.6/(0.6×10⁻³) = 1.3 mm.

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): For the convex lens alone, u = −30 cm and f₁ = +10 cm. Using the lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/10 + 1/(−30) gives 1/v = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30, so v = 15 cm. When the concave lens is placed in contact, the screen must be moved 45 cm farther, so the new image distance is v' = 15 + 45 = 60 cm. The equivalent focal length F of the combination: 1/F = 1/v' − 1/u = 1/60 − 1/(−30) = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20. So F = 20 cm. Since 1/F = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂: 1/20 = 1/10 + 1/f₂, giving 1/f₂ = 1/20 − 1/10 = −1/20. Therefore f₂ = −20 cm. The focal length of the concave lens is 20 cm. Part (a)(ii): For an equilateral prism A = 60°. Using n = sin((A + D_m)/2)/sin(A/2): √3 = sin((60 + D_m)/2)/sin30° = sin((60 + D_m)/2)/0.5. So sin((60 + D_m)/2) = √3/2. This gives (60 + D_m)/2 = 60°, so D_m = 60°. The angle of incidence at minimum deviation is i = (A + D_m)/2 = (60 + 60)/2 = 60°. Part (b)(i)(I): Fringe width β = λD/d. Rearranging: d = λD/β = (633 × 10⁻⁹ × 5.0)/(5 × 10⁻³) = 6.33 × 10⁻⁴ m ≈ 0.633 mm. Part (b)(i)(II): The first minimum is at a distance β/2 = 2.5 mm from the central maximum. Part (b)(ii): The distance between first minima on both sides of the central maximum in single-slit diffraction is 2λD/a = 2 × 650 × 10⁻⁹ × 0.60/(0.6 × 10⁻³) = 1.3 × 10⁻³ m = 1.3 mm.

(क) (i) दो बिन्दु आवेश +q और −q, x-y तल में (a, 0) तथा (−a, 0) पर रखे हैं। इन आवेशों के कारण बिन्दु (0, y) पर नेट विद्युत-क्षेत्र के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए। इस प्रकार किसी दूरस्थ बिन्दु (y >> a) पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र ज्ञात कीजिए।
(ii) भुजा 0.2 m के किसी समबाहु त्रिभुज के तीन शीर्षों A, B और C पर −2 nC, −1 nC और +5 nC के तीन बिन्दु आवेश स्थित हैं। आवेशों को A से A₁, B से B₁ तथा C से C₁ तक विस्थापित करने में किया गया कुल कार्य ज्ञात कीजिए। यहाँ A₁, B₁ और C₁ क्रमशः भुजा AB, BC और CA के मध्य-बिन्दु हैं।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Two point charges +q and −q are held at (a, 0) and (−a, 0) in x-y plane. Obtain an expression for the net electric field due to the charges at a point (0, y). Hence, find electric field at a far off point (y >> a).
(ii) Three point charges of −2 nC, −1 nC, and +5 nC are kept at the vertices A, B and C of an equilateral triangle of side 0.2 m. Find the total amount of work done in shifting the charges from A to A₁, B to B₁ and C to C₁. Here A₁, B₁ and C₁ are the midpoints of sides AB, BC and CA, respectively.

OR

(b) (i) Show that Gauss's theorem is consistent with Coulomb's law. Using it, derive an expression for the electric field due to a uniformly charged thin spherical shell of radius r at a point at a distance y from the centre of the shell such that (I) y > r, and (II) y < r.
(ii) A point charge of +2 nC is kept at the origin of a three-dimensional coordinate system. Find the type and magnitude of the charge which should be kept at (0, 0, −6m) so that the potential due to the system becomes zero at (0, 0, 2m).

key_points: (a)(i) Each charge is at distance √(a²+y²) from (0,y). The y-components of fields cancel; x-components add. E_net = 2 × (Kq/(a²+y²)) × (a/√(a²+y²)) = 2Kqa/(a²+y²)^(3/2) in −x direction (since +q at +a and −q at −a make the net field point along −x axis toward −q). For y>>a: E ≈ 2Kqa/y³ = Kp/y³ where p=2qa.

(a)(ii) Work done = change in potential energy = U_final − U_initial. Initial U_i involves all pairs at distance 0.2 m. Final U_f involves pairs at distances 0.1 m. Computing ΔU = U_f − U_i gives the work done.
(b)(i) Gauss's law gives E × 4πy² = Q/ε₀. For y>r: E = Q/(4πε₀y²) = KQ/y² (same as point charge). For y<r: no enclosed charge, E = 0.
(b)(ii) V_total at (0,0,2) = 0. K×2nC/2 + K×Q/|2−(−6)| = 0. K×1nC + K×Q/8 = 0. Q = −8 nC (negative charge of 8 nC).

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): The charge +q is at (a, 0) and −q is at (−a, 0). The point P is at (0, y). Distance from each charge to P is r = √(a² + y²). The electric field due to +q at P points away from +q, and due to −q points toward −q. The y-components of both fields are equal and opposite, so they cancel. The x-components both point in the −x direction (from +q toward the negative x-axis side, from −q attracting P toward negative x). The net field is E_net = 2 × [Kq/(a²+y²)] × [a/√(a²+y²)] = 2Kqa/(a²+y²)^(3/2) directed along the −x axis (i.e., along the direction from +q to −q, which is the dipole direction). For y >> a: E ≈ 2Kqa/y³ = Kp/y³ where p = 2qa is the dipole moment. Part (a)(ii): Initial configuration — equilateral triangle ABC of side 0.2 m with charges q_A = −2 nC, q_B = −1 nC, q_C = +5 nC. Initial potential energy U_i = K[q_Aq_B/0.2 + q_Bq_C/0.2 + q_Aq_C/0.2]. In the final configuration, A₁, B₁, C₁ are midpoints of AB, BC, CA respectively, forming a smaller equilateral triangle of side 0.1 m. U_f = K[q_Aq_B/0.1 + q_Bq_C/0.1 + q_Aq_C/0.1]. Work done W = U_f − U_i = K × (1/0.1 − 1/0.2) × [q_Aq_B + q_Bq_C + q_Aq_C] = K × 5 × [(−2)(−1) + (−1)(5) + (−2)(5)] × 10⁻¹⁸ = 9×10⁹ × 5 × [2 − 5 − 10] × 10⁻¹⁸ = 9×10⁹ × 5 × (−13) × 10⁻¹⁸ = −585 × 10⁻⁹ J = −585 nJ. Part (b)(i): Gauss's theorem states that total electric flux through a closed surface = Q_enclosed/ε₀. For a spherical shell of radius r with total charge Q: outside (y > r): Gaussian sphere of radius y encloses total charge Q, so E × 4πy² = Q/ε₀, giving E = Q/(4πε₀y²) = KQ/y², identical to Coulomb's law for a point charge. Inside (y < r): Gaussian sphere encloses no charge, so E = 0. Part (b)(ii): The +2 nC charge is at the origin (0,0,0). We need the total potential at P = (0,0,2m) to be zero. Let the unknown charge be q at (0,0,−6m). Distance from origin to P = 2 m; distance from (0,0,−6) to P = |2−(−6)| = 8 m. V_P = K×2×10⁻⁹/2 + K×q/8 = 0. Solving: K×10⁻⁹ + Kq/8 = 0 → q = −8 × 10⁻⁹ C = −8 nC. The charge must be −8 nC (negative) placed at (0, 0, −6m).
